# sonrai_custom_control (Resource)

Defines a custom control: a named group of permissions the firewall can protect or block, alongside the controls it ships with.

A custom control belongs to the whole organization, not to a root scope, and defining one takes effect as soon as it is applied. On its own it protects nothing. Attach it to an account by giving its `control_key` to `sonrai_account_protected_service` or `sonrai_account_disabled_service`; that part is staged and submitted like any other control.

A control with the same name that already exists -- made in the console, or by another configuration -- is rejected rather than adopted; import it instead.

~> **Editing the permissions of a control that is deployed needs a redeploy.** The definition changes at once, but every account it is deployed in keeps enforcing the old list until its root scope is submitted and deployed again. Reference `revision` in the `triggers` of each `sonrai_control_submission` and that happens in the same apply. The apply warns with the root scopes affected, which can include ones this configuration does not manage.

~> **A control that is attached cannot be destroyed in the same apply that detaches it.** The platform will not delete a control that is still deployed, and detaching one only takes effect once that change is submitted and deployed. Remove the attachments and apply, then remove this resource and apply again. A plan that would destroy a deployed control is rejected, naming where it is deployed, before anything is changed. Attachments that were staged and never deployed are discarded with the control.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A named group of permissions. It belongs to the whole organization and is
# defined as soon as this is applied, but protects nothing until it is attached.
resource "sonrai_custom_control" "data_destruction" {
  title       = "Data Destruction"
  cloud_type  = "aws"
  description = "Deleting buckets, tables and snapshots"

  # The complete list. Every permission is checked when planning.
  permissions = [
    "s3:DeleteBucket",
    "dynamodb:DeleteTable",
    "ec2:DeleteSnapshot",
  ]
}

# Attach it like a built-in service, by its control key. This part is staged,
# and takes effect when submitted and deployed.
resource "sonrai_account_protected_service" "data_destruction" {
  root_scope  = "aws/r-abcd"
  resource_id = "123456789012"
  control_key = sonrai_custom_control.data_destruction.control_key
}

resource "sonrai_control_submission" "firewall" {
  root_scope = "aws/r-abcd"

  triggers = {
    protect = sonrai_account_protected_service.data_destruction.revision
    # Moves when the permissions of the deployed control are edited, which is
    # what redeploys them. Without it the old list stays in force.
    control = sonrai_custom_control.data_destruction.revision
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cloud_type` (String) Cloud the control is for: `aws` or `gcp`. Forces replacement.
- `description` (String) What the control is for. Shown wherever the control is listed.
- `permissions` (Set of String) Permissions the control covers, such as `s3:DeleteBucket`. This is the complete list: an edit replaces it. Every one must exist for `cloud_type`, which the plan checks. For GCP, use the `service.googleapis.com/resource.verb` form. At most 1000.
- `title` (String) Name of the control. Letters, numbers, spaces, hyphens, underscores and periods, starting with a letter or number. The platform derives `control_key` from it by lower-casing it and removing spaces, so a title that gives a different key is a different control and forces replacement. Changing only its case or spacing renames the control in place. It cannot match a built-in control.

### Optional

- `delete_timeout` (String) How long destroy waits for a deployment that is already removing the control to finish before giving up. Defaults to `30m`, and cannot exceed `24h`.

### Read-Only

- `control_key` (String) Key the platform gave the control. Use it as the `control_key` of `sonrai_account_protected_service` or `sonrai_account_disabled_service` to attach the control to an account.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the form `cloud_type:control_key`.
- `revision` (String) Opaque value that changes when the control needs redeploying: when the permissions of a deployed control are edited, and while such an edit is still waiting to be deployed. Reference it in the `triggers` of each `sonrai_control_submission` whose root scope uses the control.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Import ID: cloud_type:control_key. Find the key with the
# sonrai_custom_controls data source. The resource is authoritative for the
# permission list, so write all of them or the next apply removes the rest.
import {
  to = sonrai_custom_control.data_destruction
  id = "aws:datadestruction"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import ID: cloud_type:control_key.
terraform import sonrai_custom_control.data_destruction 'aws:datadestruction'
```
